messages:
maria: FYI — AcadiaHealth SOW negotiation tomorrow. They asked for Dedicated pool commit guidance. Quick thread to align on sizing + billing risks.

kevin: Do we have their 30-day P50/P95 throughput traces? Last 14d avg ~420k tokens/min but with huge spikes during batch jobs.

sophie: Uploaded an aggregated profile to GCS: gs://redwood-telemetry/acadia/throughput-14d.csv — includes prompt-length buckets and seq-len hist.

ajay: Main question: do we present commits as reserved GPUs or committed throughput? For Dedicated sales wants a simple "N GPUs" number but engineering thinks committed tokens/sec is clearer.

kevin: Reminder: under the hood we commit GPU-hours and expose a mapping to "committed throughput units". Example mapping we use internally: 1 commit unit ≈ 100 tokens/sec sustained (depends on model and quantization).

maria: Need a short worked example for the contract. Show how to go from customer 99th percentile token/sec -> GPUs -> monthly GPU-hours -> cost. Also call out EU vs US pricing delta.

ajay: Quick calc from their profile: peak 30d P99 ≈ 7.5k tokens/sec. If A100-80 (our baseline for redwood-7b quantized) gives ~2k tokens/sec per GPU on their mixes, then 4 GPUs ≈ 8k tps. Add 20% buffer -> 5 GPUs.

kevin: So monthly reserved GPU-hours = 5 GPUs * 24 * 30 = 3600 GPU-hours. Apply our Dedicated rate and you'll get the committed line item. Show both list price and committed-discount price in the quote.

sophie: Also flag: last month we saw an egress/billing spike for their test cluster in eu-west-1 — billing-bot flagged unexpected NAT gateway + cross-region logs costs.

billing-bot: Flagged incident: AWS-8890. July 2025 spike = ~$18k attributed to NAT gateway + cross-region CloudWatch logs transfer when telemetry export was pointed at us-east-1. Root cause was misconfigured metrics export. Ticket open, billing credit in progress.

maria: Important constraint: Acadia requires EU-only data residency. That pushes us to reserve capacity in eu-west-1 where spot of A100-80 is 15% more expensive and immediate availability is limited. We should surface that tradeoff.

ajay: If we commit EU GPUs we should plan a 2–3 week procurement ramp. Ops-bot — can you check immediate pool availability?

ops-bot: quota-check: eu-west-1 available A100-80 immediate pools = 4, procurement lead time to 8 additional = 14-21 days. Confirmed.

kevin: Suggest commitment structure for the quote: baseline reserved GPUs to cover 99% traffic + burst buffer via autoscale (pay-as-you-go) with overage multiplier. Example contract wording: "Committed GPUs cover sustained baseline; bursts above baseline billed at 1.6x per-hour rate".

maria: Also call out upgrade path: if they want to convert burst to reserve later we can amortize procurement.

sophie: Action item — produce a concise commit-sizing doc for sales: 1) measurement & assumptions, 2) conversion formula, 3) cost table (EU vs US), 4) procurement timeline, 5) billing caveats (egress/NAT/CR exports).

kevin: I'll draft. Will include the formula snippet and a sample commit manifest they can paste into the console. Target: EOD tomorrow.

maria: Please include a short example YAML we can show in the quote UI.

maria: ```yaml
commit:
  region: eu-west-1
  model_family: redwood-7b
  reserved_gpus: 5
  guaranteed_qps: 8000
  overage_policy: 'pay-as-you-go beyond reserved at 1.6x'
```

ajay: I'll run a quick 3-run bench on their exact prompt mix and post numbers (tokens/sec + p95 lat).

kevin: Also note: if legal insists on 99.99% coverage we need to add 1–2 extra GPUs for safety which changes the economics materially. Will call that out.

sophie: tagging @billing-bot to make sure the NAT/egress issue is fully closed before we sign.

billing-bot: Confirmed: AWS-8890 has a pending credit and export config fix deployed. Monitoring for residuals.

maria: Great. Quick todo list: (1) Kevin: draft commit-sizing doc + cost table; (2) Ajay: perf numbers per GPU; (3) Ops: confirm procurement ETA and quotas; (4) Billing: confirm credit applied and EU export config fixed.

kevin: Working on it. Will post draft link when ready. :thumbsup:
